Figure 20. Ingot and wafer production costs (excluding polysilicon) by point of origin in 2024 All countries outside China have higher EPC costs. The most important reason is scale. Some ingot and wafer plants in China already produce 50 GW of wafers per year (or more), while dc typical plants elsewhere are around one-tenth that size. In addition, facility designs differ owing to different local permitting requirements, and the United States and Europe have higher EPC labor and management costs as well as significantly more expensive building materials. Wafer cost of goods sold calculations are most sensitive to labor and utility rates. Labor costs in the United States and Europe are highest because of higher annual labor rates and possibly more total employees (if using more shifts). We assume energy intensity is the same for all locations, but local utility rates vary widely. High utility rates are particularly challenging for Europe. Outside China, an investment in new ingot and wafer capacity at the minimum 5-GW scale dc equated to a capital raise of $600–$800 million in 2024. Global spot prices of $0.15–$0.20 per wafer ($18–$25/kW ) were not uncommon in 2024, even including the polysilicon. Such prices dc would not cover the cumulative cash costs for polysilicon-plus-wafer production. In 2024, we estimate financing costs were lowest in China, ASEAN, and India and highest in the United States and Europe owing to attractive returns offered from competing, lower-risk investments. Higher CapEx and interest rates in the United States and Europe make financing and profit costs much higher in those locations than in China, ASEAN, and India.
